title: Cofibrant resolution preserving a poset filtration
statement:
Use small simplicial categories and the Dwyer--Kan model structure of [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property], and Kan fibrations and weak equivalences of simplicial sets as in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Fix containing universes. Let $A$ be a small partially ordered set and $C$ a small simplicial category with a function $d:\operatorname{Ob}C\to A$ such that $C(x,y)=\varnothing$ whenever $d(x)\nleq d(y)$. For $a\in A$, let $C_{\leq a}$ be the full simplicial subcategory on objects $x$ with $d(x)\leq a$; inclusions define an ordinary diagram $A\to\mathrm{sCat}$. Suppose $\mathrm{sCat}^{A}$ has the projective model structure, with objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations. Then there is a simplicial functor $f:C'\to C$, bijective on objects, such that each map
$$C'(x,y)\longrightarrow C(fx,fy)$$
is a trivial Kan fibration, $C'(x,y)=\varnothing$ if $d(fx)\nleq d(fy)$, and the diagram $a\mapsto C'_{\leq a}$ is projectively cofibrant. Here $C'_{\leq a}$ is the full subcategory on $d(fx)\leq a$, and projectively cofibrant means that its map from the initial diagram has the left lifting property against every objectwise trivial fibration of diagrams. In particular $f$ and all $C'_{\leq a}\to C_{\leq a}$ are Dwyer--Kan equivalences. No filteredness, well-foundedness, nonemptiness or existence of a largest element is assumed for $A$.

source.place: Definition A.3.5.7 and Lemma A.3.5.9, printed pp.894--895 (PDF pp.911--912). Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-category theorem.

proof.text: Put $O=\operatorname{Ob}C$, with its given grading $d$, and work with identity-on-$O$ functors. The fixed-object category $\mathrm{sCat}_O$ exists and is cocomplete by [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. Its initial object $D_0$ has just the identity arrows. For each $x,y\in O$ with $d(x)\leq d(y)$ and each $n\geq0$, take the map $F^O_{x,y}(\partial\Delta^n)\to F^O_{x,y}(\Delta^n)$, using the free-arrow adjunction [lem-coef-fixed-object-free-arrow-adjunction]. These maps form a small set $I_d$. Start with the identity-preserving map $D_0\to C$.

source.place: Definition A.3.5.7 and Lemma A.3.5.9; explicit fixed-object boundary-cell argument by the worker, using the cited DAG statements. Archival HTT WANTED.

proof.text: The domains of $I_d$ are small for the countable cell construction. Indeed, along a chain of identity-on-$O$ enriched functors, take the colimit of each mapping simplicial set. Composition of two representatives is computed at a common stage; associativity, units, and the equality criterion are checked at a later common stage. This gives the colimit in $\mathrm{sCat}_O$. By the free-arrow adjunction, a map from a domain of $I_d$ into that colimit is just a map from $\partial\Delta^n$ to one mapping set. For $n>0$ a map from the boundary is specified by its $n+1$ face simplices of dimension $n-1$, with the finitely many equations on their pairwise intersections (for $n=1$ the two vertices have empty intersection). Thus these face images and equations occur at one finite stage; equalities of two such maps likewise occur at one later stage. For $n=0$ the domain boundary is empty and this assertion is immediate. Thus these Hom functors preserve the colimits of the countable chains in question, exactly the $\kappa=\aleph_0$ hypothesis of [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization].

source.place: Definition A.3.5.7 and Lemma A.3.5.9; explicit fixed-object boundary-cell argument by the worker, using the cited DAG statements. Archival HTT WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization] to $D_0\to C$ and $I_d$. Concretely, at stage $m+1$ attach one free $n$-simplex for every commutative square $\partial\Delta^n\to D_m(x,y)$ over $\Delta^n\to C(x,y)$ with $d(x)\leq d(y)$, and take the colimit at $\omega$. All squares at a stage form a small set. Write $C'=D_\omega$ and $f:C'\to C$. All stages have object set $O$ and $f$ is identity on $O$. By [lem-coef-scat-fixed-object-pushout-comparison], each fixed-object attachment is also the pushout along $U(\partial\Delta^n)\to U(\Delta^n)$ in variable-object simplicial categories, including when $x=y$. Coproduct attachments can be ordered as a small sequence of single attachments, whose universal property is the same.

source.place: Definition A.3.5.7 and Lemma A.3.5.9; explicit fixed-object boundary-cell argument by the worker, using the cited DAG statements. Archival HTT WANTED.

proof.text: At every stage $D_m(w,z)=\varnothing$ if $d(w)\nleq d(z)$. This holds for $D_0$. For a single attachment from $x$ to $y$, use the word presentation in [lem-coef-scat-arrow-cell-word-filtration]: each old letter goes between nondecreasing grades, and the new letter has $d(x)\leq d(y)$. Hence every nonempty word goes from a grade to a greater or equal grade. The reduction relations preserve endpoints. The same assertion survives successive attachments and the mapping-set colimits described in Step 2. The right factor from Step 3 has the right lifting property against $I_d$; by the free-arrow adjunction this gives the boundary lifting property for $C'(x,y)\to C(x,y)$ whenever $d(x)\leq d(y)$. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] these are trivial Kan fibrations. For the remaining pairs both mapping sets are empty, so the map is an isomorphism and also a trivial Kan fibration.

source.place: Definition A.3.5.7 and Lemma A.3.5.9; explicit fixed-object boundary-cell argument by the worker, using the cited DAG statements. Archival HTT WANTED.

proof.text: Fix $a\in A$. In the same word formula, a word whose target has grade at most $a$ has every intermediate object of grade at most $a$, since its grades are nondecreasing. Thus an attachment from $x$ to $y$ affects the full subcategory on grades at most $a$ exactly by that same free attachment if $d(y)\leq a$; if $d(y)\nleq a$, it leaves every mapping set between these objects unchanged. In the first case $d(x)\leq a$ too. Relations in the word presentation also stay within these objects, so they introduce no extra identifications from outside the subcategory. Consequently $a\mapsto D_m{}_{\leq a}$ is built from the discrete-object diagram by cells each present precisely at $a\geq d(y)$. This description commutes with limit stages by the mapping-set colimit construction of Step 2. It is a direct restriction of the cited word formula, requiring no well-ordering of $A$.

source.place: Definition A.3.5.7 and Lemma A.3.5.9; explicit fixed-object boundary-cell argument by the worker, using the cited DAG statements. Archival HTT WANTED.

proof.text: To prove projective cofibrancy, let $p:X\to Y$ be an objectwise trivial fibration of $A$-diagrams and let $g:(a\mapsto C'_{\leq a})\to Y$ be a natural transformation. In the Dwyer--Kan structure the generating cofibrations are $\varnothing\to\{0\}$ and $U(\partial\Delta^n)\to U(\Delta^n)$ by [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting] and [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property]; hence each $p_a$ lifts against these maps. For each $x\in O$, lift $g_{d(x)}(x)$ to an object of $X_{d(x)}$ using the first generator. At every $a\geq d(x)$ take its image under the transition functor. Naturality of $g$ makes these choices a lift on the discrete-object diagram. Suppose a compatible lift is defined at an earlier cellular stage. A cell $\partial\Delta^n\to\Delta^n$ from $x$ to $y$ first occurs at $b=d(y)$ by Step 5. Its boundary already maps to $X_b$, its whole simplex maps to $Y_b$, and the two agree after $p_b$. Lift the corresponding $U$-square at $b$; send the chosen simplex at every $a\geq b$ to its image under $X_b\to X_a$. By Step 5 and [lem-coef-scat-fixed-object-pushout-comparison], at each $a\geq b$ the attachment is the pushout along $U(\partial\Delta^n)\to U(\Delta^n)$ in variable-object simplicial categories, so functors out of it into $X_a$ are the old functor plus a compatible simplex; this extends the lift, and makes it natural. At a limit take the compatible colimit map. This constructs a natural lift against every $p$, proving the asserted left lifting property.

source.place: Definition A.3.5.7 and Lemma A.3.5.9; explicit fixed-object boundary-cell argument by the worker, using the cited DAG statements. Archival HTT WANTED.

proof.text: Each restriction $C'_{\leq a}\to C_{\leq a}$ is identity on its object set and a weak homotopy equivalence on every mapping set by Step 4, just as $f$ is. These maps therefore induce fully faithful and bijective-on-objects functors on the categories of path components, hence equivalences. The definition in [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property] now gives all the claimed Dwyer--Kan equivalences. If $A$ is empty then $O$ is empty and every construction is the empty category or empty diagram. An empty lower subcategory causes no cells or choices at that index. Loops and objects of equal grade are already allowed by the free-arrow and pushout comparison statements. No directedness, well-foundedness, or largest element was used.
